points.t: Bright, beefy-red, moist plaques in a skin fold, with satellite papules or pustules beyond the edge.
Opportunistic Candida albicans overgrowth in warm, wet, occluded folds.
Keep the fold dry, then a topical imidazole or nystatin. Address the risk factors.
Undiagnosed diabetes or immunosuppression, and flexural psoriasis or tinea that will not respond.

points: **Beefy-red, macerated plaques** in folds, often glistening or eroded.
**Satellite papules and pustules** beyond the main edge. This is the key sign.
Peripheral peeling scale at the margin.
In the groin, Candida often **involves the scrotum**, which tinea tends to spare.
if recurrent or there are other risk features.
Usually clinical, based on the site and satellite lesions.
Take a swab or scrapings for yeast if uncertain, recurrent or not responding. Swab for bacteria if secondary infection is suspected.

cards.name: Irritant (simple) intertrigo
cards.clue: Friction and moisture redness without satellites; mirror-image on both sides of the fold

cards.name: Flexural (inverse) psoriasis
cards.clue: Sharply defined salmon-pink plaque, no satellites; psoriasis at other sites or nails

cards.name: Tinea cruris
cards.clue: Arcuate scaly active edge spreading onto the thigh; scrotum usually spared

cards.name: Erythrasma
cards.clue: Brown-red, finely scaly patch; coral-red under Wood’s light (Corynebacterium)

cards.name: Seborrhoeic dermatitis
cards.clue: Greasy scale; also scalp and face

cards.name: Hailey–Hailey disease / pemphigus vegetans (rare)
cards.clue: Chronic, eroded, recurrent fold disease that does not respond. Refer

points: **Imidazole** (clotrimazole or miconazole) or **nystatin**. Continue until 1–2 weeks after clearance.

For very inflamed folds, a short course of a combination with mild steroid (e.g. hydrocortisone with clotrimazole or miconazole) is sometimes used. Follow the local formulary and limit to about 7 days.
**Fluconazole** for severe or recalcitrant disease. Check interactions and pregnancy status.

items.t: Recurrent or extensive candida: **screen for diabetes** and consider immunosuppression.
No response to an adequate course: reconsider the diagnosis (psoriasis, tinea, erythrasma) and take samples.
Spreading cellulitis, fever or a systemically unwell patient: escalate.

pearls.t: **Satellites mean Candida.** No satellites and a very sharp edge suggests flexural psoriasis.
Treatment fails without moisture control. Make the drying advice practical and specific.
OTC clotrimazole is a sensible first pharmacy intervention for limited disease.
In finger-web disease, ask about wet work and rings.
The toe-web ‘dermatophytosis complex’ is often a **mixed** yeast, dermatophyte and bacterial picture. It needs thorough drying plus the right antimicrobial.
KOH-negative fold rash, or one that keeps coming back? Work through [intertrigo and the flexural differential](condition:intertrigo).

quiz.a: Bright, beefy-red, moist plaques in a skin fold, with satellite papules or pustules beyond the edge.
Opportunistic Candida albicans overgrowth in warm, wet, occluded folds.

quiz.a: Recurrent or extensive candida: **screen for diabetes** and consider immunosuppression.
